title: Skyroot's Orbital Rocket Launch Exposes Huge 'Missing Middle' in Deep-Tech Venture Capital!
summary: Following Skyroot Aerospace's successful Vikram-1 orbital mission, financial analysts highlighted systemic funding gaps facing capital-intensive hardware startups transitioning from prototype to production. Indian deep-tech captured only $1.65 billion in 2025 compared to over $147 billion raised in the US.
raw_text: So check this out—Skyroot Aerospace made history by launching the Vikram-1 orbital rocket, making India one of only three countries with private orbital launch capabilities! But here's the wild part: industry experts are warning that Skyroot's victory is an exception in a deep-tech funding system that is fundamentally broken. Hardware founders are running into what analysts call the 'missing middle.' You can get early seed grants to build a prototype in a lab, but when you need tens of millions for industrial tooling, rocket factories, and inventory, traditional venture capital completely freezes up. In fact, Indian deep-tech raised just $1.65 billion last year compared to $147 billion in the US and $81 billion in China. Without major structural credit guarantees and risk-sharing reforms, brilliant hardware startups will starve before ever reaching commercial scale. Deep tech needs real capital, not just seed checks!
